title: Jensen Huang on character, resilience and first principles: building NVIDIA through the AI phase shift
summary: Jensen explains why NVIDIA reinvented the whole computer stack for deep learning, why AI is an iPhone moment and a new industrial revolution of producing intelligence, and how company character, forged by 15 years of adversity, drives lasting success. He closes with advice to think from first principles.

principles.text: When a new computing model appears, rethink the whole stack from chips to applications instead of patching the old one.
principles.quote: what is the implications to um everything about computer science from chips to systems to operating systems to Data Centers to networking to the algorithms all the way to applications

principles.text: Platform shifts arrive slowly, then abruptly like a phase change, and each one makes computers easier to program.
principles.quote: at first slowly and all of a sudden abruptly just like the just like water turning to ice or water turning to Vapor

principles.text: Innovation is about timing: the technology brews for years, and innovators realize the time is now and industrialize it.
principles.quote: the innovators are the ones that realize the timing is now and to jump on it and um industrialized it and turned it into a really great product

principles.text: Approach hard new things with 'how hard can it be?' and learn the missing skills; reason from first principles.
principles.quote: we started with the attitude how hard can it be and and so if it's a solvable problem how hard can it be and we reasoned about everything from first principles

principles.text: A company's character, meaning resilience, agility and willingness to suffer, is what makes it succeed in the long run.
principles.quote: the character of a company um is what makes it ultimately successful and you know how resilient is it um how does it deal with adversity

principles.text: Think for yourself from first principles; you can learn to love what you do rather than hunting for something to love.
principles.quote: think for yourself think from first principles
